name: Kingdom of Warri

summary.text: The Itsekiri kingdom of the western Delta creeks, founded by Ginuwa, a prince of Benin. Its Olu adopted Christianity through Portuguese missionaries in the 16th century and grew rich as a middleman in the river trade. After 1848 no Olu was crowned for 88 years and merchant governors ran the rivers; the British crushed Nana Olomu at Ebrohimi in 1894.

snapshots.title: Ginuwa founds the kingdom
snapshots.text: Ginuwa, a prince of Benin, settles among the Itsekiri and founds the royal seat at Ode-Itsekiri.

snapshots.title: A Christian kingdom in the Delta
snapshots.text: An Olu is baptised Sebastião by 1597; his son Domingos studies in Portugal and marries a Portuguese noblewoman. Warri trades cloth, palm products and enslaved people.

snapshots.title: The interregnum
snapshots.text: Olu Akengbuwa dies and no successor is agreed. For 88 years governors of the river, chosen from merchant houses, control the Itsekiri trade.

snapshots.title: Ebrohimi falls
snapshots.text: Nana Olomu, Governor of the Benin River, resists British control of the palm-oil trade; British forces take his stronghold at Ebrohimi.

today.text: The monarchy was restored in 1936. The Olu of Warri reigns at Ode-Itsekiri and Warri, Delta State.
today.title: Olu of Warri

reviewNotes: Ode-Itsekiri and Ebrohimi points are approximate.
Itsekiri, Urhobo and Ijaw claims over Warri are politically sensitive; this file only shows where the kingdom's towns were.
